usage.callShape: GET https://signalsfeed.com/api/v1/sentiment?ids=<uuid1>,<uuid2> (x402, ~$0.01/call, up to 20 signals). Free discovery first: GET https://signalsfeed.com/api/v1/sentiment?quality_status=premium&limit=20 (no payment) to obtain purchasable signal UUIDs.
usage.outputShape: body.signals[] — each has claim, canonical_claim, subject/predicate/object, confidence (0-1), credibility_score (0-1), entities[], keywords[], numeric_value/numeric_unit, evidence[] (source_url, publisher, excerpt), supporting_articles[]. Also body.count and body.format="full".
quirks: Paying with NO ids= (or other free-discovery params) returns only teaser metadata, not full signals — to actually unlock content you MUST pass ids=<comma-separated UUIDs>.
Get the UUIDs FIRST from the free discovery surface: GET ...?quality_status=premium&limit=20 returns signals[].id of purchasable records at no cost (no x402).
Only quality_status=premium IDs are purchasable; paid call caps at 20 signals regardless of limit.
Single endpoint serves both free discovery (teasers, top_topics, preview) and the paid full-signal unlock; behavior depends entirely on query params.
Domains are limited to ai / semiconductor / macro.
usage.guide: Two-step flow. First call the free discovery surface GET https://signalsfeed.com/api/v1/sentiment?quality_status=premium&limit=20 (no payment) and collect the signals[].id UUIDs you want. Then make the paid x402 call GET https://signalsfeed.com/api/v1/sentiment?ids=<comma-separated UUIDs> which costs ~$0.01 USDC on Base and returns up to 20 full signals. Read results from body.signals[]: use claim/canonical_claim for the headline, confidence and credibility_score for trust, and evidence[].source_url for citations. Paying without ids= only returns teasers, so always supply ids.
